attempts.summary: Built a WireGuard site-to-site tunnel between node1 (VyOS) and node2 (OPNsense), the two routers facing each other across the transit network, joining their private networks (node3 behind node1, node4 behind node2). node3 (10.10.10.2/24) and node4 (10.20.20.2/24) now reach each other by their private addresses, with all inter-router traffic traveling encrypted inside the WireGuard tunnel (verified via tcpdump showing only UDP/51820 on the transit link). Topology discovered via arping: node1 eth1 <-> node2 vtnet1 (transit, 10.99.99.0/30), node1 eth2 <-> node3 ens7 (private net A, 10.10.10.0/24), node2 vtnet2 <-> node4 ens7 (private net B, 10.20.20.0/24). Configured VyOS via its native `configure/commit/save` workflow (wg0 10.255.255.1/30, static route to 10.20.20.0/24 via wg0, forward/input firewall rules) and OPNsense via config.xml + configd (opt1/opt2 interface assignments, WireGuard server+client instances via the built-in WireGuard menu, and — critically — assigned wg0 as interface opt3 since OPNsense's legacy filter compiler cannot resolve pf rules against the dynamic 'wireguard' interface group, only against assigned interfaces). node3/node4 got persistent static addressing and cross-subnet routes via systemd-networkd .network files (overriding the platform's blanket en*/eth* DHCP match). All four nodes were then restarted one at a time (VyOS reboot, OPNsense reboot, Ubuntu reboot x2), each verified via a changed OS-native boot marker (Linux boot_id, FreeBSD kern.boottime), and full private-to-private connectivity plus WireGuard handshake/tunnel state was reverified after each restart, confirming the configuration is persistent and survives reboot.
